standard_prerequisites.use: The topological invariance theorem of the same chapter (theorem-topological-invariance, already collected as S3-spaces-topological-invariance) supplying the equivalence, and descent results for being a scheme and for affineness along integral universally bijective morphisms (Limits of Spaces); cited inputs with the argument written in the retained span.

core_obligations: Reformulate the restriction claim as: V in Y_spaces_etale is a scheme (affine) iff V x_Y X is.
Check the projection V x_Y X -> V is integral, universally injective and surjective.
Conclude scheme-ness and affineness of V from the cited descent results in Limits of Spaces.

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the restriction statement to descent of scheme-ness and affineness along the base change map.
Apply the integral universally bijective descent lemmas to conclude.

difficulty_reason: In the situation of the chapter's topological invariance theorem (a universal submersive integral universally injective morphism X -> Y), the equivalence of big etale topoi Y_spaces_etale -> X_spaces_etale restricts to equivalences on the small etale sites Y_etale -> X_etale and on the affine etale sites Y_affine_etale -> X_affine_etale. The retained proof is written out: the claim is exactly that an object V of Y_spaces_etale is a scheme (resp. affine scheme) if and only if V x_Y X is; the base change V x_Y X -> V is integral, universally injective and surjective as a base change of X -> Y, so the assertion follows from the Limits of Spaces lemma that being a scheme descends along integral universally bijective maps and the proposition that affineness descends there. Retained author proof at lines 1424-1433.

dedup.scope: Label single-chapter (absent from stacks-more-morphisms). This is the small-site (schemes and affine schemes) restriction corollary of the topological invariance theorem.
